title: Max Increase to Keep City Skyline
summary: Given an n x n matrix where each element represents the height of a building in a city block, determine the maximum total increase in the height of any building such that the city's skyline, viewed from any of the four cardinal directions (north, east, south, west), remains unchanged.
statement: Given an n x n matrix where each element represents the height of a building in a city block, determine the maximum total increase in the height of any building such that the city's skyline, viewed from any of the four cardinal directions (north, east, south, west), remains unchanged.
constraints: grid is a nonempty square matrix of nonnegative heights.
Increasing buildings must preserve every row maximum and column maximum.
hints: A cell may rise only to the smaller of its row and column skyline limits.
Compute all row and column maxima first.
Each independent increase reaches the greatest value that preserves both directional skylines.
editorial: Each independent increase reaches the greatest value that preserves both directional skylines.

tests.explanation: Raising each cell to the smaller of its row and column maxima adds thirty-five.
A single building cannot increase without changing both skylines.
